title: tcdf
summary: Evaluate the Student's t cumulative distribution function.

gpu_support.notes: GPU arrays are supported. When no native provider hook is available, RunMat gathers through the owning provider, evaluates on the host, and restores the result to that provider.

description: `tcdf(x,nu)` evaluates the Student's t cumulative distribution function. `tcdf(x,nu,"upper")` returns the complementary upper-tail probability.
behaviors: `x` and `nu` may be scalars or compatible-size single- or double-precision arrays.
Scalar inputs broadcast over matching-size array inputs.
Single-precision input produces single-precision output; otherwise the result is double precision.
In RunMat mode, typed-integer and logical inputs are available as extensions. Integer values must be exactly representable as double before evaluation.
Nonpositive or `NaN` degrees of freedom produce `NaN` elementwise.
`nu = Inf` uses the standard normal distribution.

faqs.question: Does tcdf support upper-tail probabilities?
faqs.answer: Yes. Pass `"upper"` as the final argument to compute the complementary tail.

faqs.question: Can I use integer arrays with `tcdf`?
faqs.answer: RunMat mode accepts all eight integer classes when every value is exactly representable as double. MATLAB-compatible mode accepts the documented single- and double-precision forms.

faqs.question: What happens to a GPU result when RunMat uses a host fallback?
faqs.answer: The result is copied back to the exact provider that owns the input, with single or double precision preserved.
